cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and what you chose is standing.
cells.act: stand firm in the material hardship
cells.ask: Pick the one hard chore that's been waiting, and carry it through on your own two feet, without asking anyone to check on you. Then set the pen down.
cells.core:
You picked a direction and you stayed with it. The thing you set out to bring through is here now, standing, and you held the line until it landed. Steering like that is not force — you said this and meant it, and you kept meaning it through the stretches that took everything you had. The completion is real, and it belongs to you.

Finish one task on your own staying power, no check-in required. That isn't a demand to carry everything alone forever. It's a chance to feel your own weight under the load once more, so the strength is known to you and not just spent. What you've held stands done.

cells.tense: You are bracing at a completion that hasn't been written in yet.
cells.act: let the feeling in without deciding what it is
cells.ask: Find a spot with nothing to hold and no next thing lined up. Let what shows up arrive, and when the urge to decide rises, wait one breath.
cells.core:
The finish line keeps moving further out, and the steering has tightened into bracing. You're trying to write the ending before the material has spoken — deciding what it will be, guarding against how it could go wrong, pushing the timeline because not-yet-known feels like standing on nothing. The ability to direct is still here; the pen is gripped so hard the page can't show you anything.

Sit with what arrives, with nothing to hold and no next thing lined up, and when the urge to decide rises, wait one breath. You don't have to name it. Notice what the not-knowing does in your body, and stay there a minute. Choosing from clarity comes back when the heart has room to receive before the hand reaches for the pen.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed, waiting to be let through.
cells.act: make the first cut of seeing and stop there
cells.ask: Go to the thing you once chose and finished, and describe what is actually there in five plain lines. Don't decide what it means or add what it should have been.
cells.core:
The direction was chosen, and some part of you is still waiting for permission to have arrived. Looking back at what was built, the eye slides off it — too small, too flawed, not what was meant, so it doesn't count. The ability to see it clearly is here. It just isn't being aimed at what's actually there, and the steering has gone quiet for lack of anything solid to set it on.

Make the first cut of seeing and stop there. Go to the thing you once chose and finished, and describe what is actually there in five plain lines. No conclusions, no corrections, no inventory of what it should have been. Seeing what's present, before naming what it means, is the beginning of clarity — and direction comes back when the eye has something real to rest on.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room where you're already writing.
cells.act: notice what is before your eyes before naming it
cells.ask: Before the next ordinary choice today, look at what's actually there — not your read of it — and name what you notice before you name what it is. Once is enough.
cells.core:
You are directing the whole thing — the effort, the order, the finish — and your account gives circumstance the credit. The steering is happening in you while the timing and the way things had to go take the bow. You're running the room and speaking of it as if the room ran you, so the part of you doing the aiming rarely gets seen, not even by you.

Notice what is before your eyes before naming it. Before the next ordinary choice today, look at the actual situation — not your read of it — and name what you notice before you name what it is. Just once. Before you were carrying the whole thing through, you were someone who could see what was in front of them. See one thing clearly, and the hand on the pen shows up as yours.
